title: The vacant judgment-seat
summary: After Moronihah had established peace between the Nephites and Lamanites, the judgment-seat was vacant and contention arose over who should fill it.

explicit_facts.text: In the forty-second year of the judges, Moronihah had established peace between the Nephites and the Lamanites.
No one filled the judgment-seat, and contention arose over who should fill it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people can be shown disputing over the vacant judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and appearance of the judgment-seat and the identities or appearance of the disputants are unspecified.

narration.text: there began to be a contention again among the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moronihah’s peace is prior context, not a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Moronihah establishing peace in this scene.
Do not invent the disputants’ words.

title: Helaman appointed
summary: The people appointed Helaman, son of Helaman, to fill the judgment-seat.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman, son of Helaman, was appointed to fill the judgment-seat by the voice of the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman may be shown among the people at his appointment.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, appointment procedure, and appearance of the people are unspecified.

narration.text: appointed to fill the judgment-seat, by the voice of the people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent ceremony or exact words spoken by the people.

title: Gadianton becomes leader of the band
summary: Kishkumen lay in wait to destroy Helaman, supported by a band that had covenanted to conceal his wickedness. Gadianton became the band's leader and flattered its members and Kishkumen with a conditional offer of power and authority. Kishkumen sought to destroy Helaman.

explicit_facts.text: Kishkumen had murdered Pahoran before these events; he lay in wait to destroy Helaman and was supported by his band, which had covenanted that no one should know his wickedness.
Gadianton was expert in words and in the secret work of murder and robbery, and became leader of Kishkumen's band.
Gadianton flattered the band and Kishkumen, offering its members power and authority if they placed him in the judgment-seat. Kishkumen sought to destroy Helaman.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gadianton, Kishkumen, and unnamed band members may be shown together; no specific meeting or ritual is described.
unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, clothing, and surroundings are unspecified.

narration.text: there was one Gadianton, who was exceedingly expert in many words, and also in his craft, to carry on the secret work of murder and of robbery;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The offer in verse 5 is conditional; the verses do not say Gadianton obtained the judgment-seat. Pahoran's murder is prior context.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Pahoran's murder as a current event.
Do not invent Gadianton's spoken words, the covenant's wording, a ritual, or an attack on Helaman.

title: The servant meets Kishkumen
summary: Kishkumen went toward the judgment-seat to destroy Helaman. Helaman’s servant, who had previously learned the band’s plans through disguise, met Kishkumen and gave him a sign. Kishkumen revealed his desire to be conducted to the judgment-seat to murder Helaman. The servant invited him to go there.

explicit_facts.text: Kishkumen went toward the judgment-seat to destroy Helaman.
One of Helaman’s servants had been out by night and had learned the band’s plans through disguise.
The servant met Kishkumen and gave him a sign.
Kishkumen revealed that he wanted the servant to conduct him to the judgment-seat so he could murder Helaman.
The servant learned that the band’s secret aims included murder, robbery, and gaining power, then invited Kishkumen to go to the judgment-seat.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Kishkumen and the servant can be shown meeting while Kishkumen is on his way toward the judgment-seat.
unspecified_visual_details: The meeting place and time are unspecified.
The form of the sign is unspecified.
The servant’s earlier disguise is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let us go forth unto the judgment-seat.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Helaman’s servant

narration.text: as he went forth towards the judgment-seat to destroy Helaman
one of the servants of Helaman, having been out by night, and having obtained, through disguise, a knowledge of those plans
he gave unto him a sign

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The servant’s night outing and acquisition of knowledge through disguise are prior actions reported by Mormon, not events occurring during this meeting.
Kishkumen’s desire is reported, not quoted as speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the earlier night outing or disguise as part of this meeting.
Do not show Helaman physically present.
Do not specify the sign or invent a disguise.
Do not add dialogue for Kishkumen or claim the servant joined the band.

title: Kishkumen is killed
summary: As Kishkumen and the servant went toward the judgment-seat, the servant stabbed Kishkumen, who fell dead without a groan.

explicit_facts.text: The servant stabbed Kishkumen to the heart, and Kishkumen fell dead without a groan.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The stabbing may be depicted without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact place and weapon’s appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: did stab Kishkumen even to the heart

prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood, wounds, gore, or an unmentioned struggle.

title: The servant reports
summary: The servant ran and told Helaman all he had seen, heard, and done.

explicit_facts.text: The servant ran and told Helaman all the things he had seen, heard, and done.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The servant may be shown reporting to Helaman.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and the content of the report are unspecified.

narration.text: he ran and told Helaman all the things which he had seen

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the report’s wording or details.

title: Helaman sends to take the band
summary: Helaman sent forth to take a band of robbers and secret murderers so they might be executed according to the law.

explicit_facts.text: Helaman sent forth to take a band of robbers and secret murderers.
The stated purpose was that they might be executed according to the law.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Helaman may be shown sending others to take the band.
unspecified_visual_details: The people sent, location, and form of the order are unspecified.

narration.text: Helaman did send forth to take this band of robbers and secret murderers, that they might be executed according to the law.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the band's capture or execution; neither is narrated as having occurred.

title: Gadianton and the band flee
summary: When Kishkumen did not return, Gadianton feared destruction and caused his band to follow him. They fled by a secret way into the wilderness, and Helaman’s searchers could not find them.

explicit_facts.text: When Kishkumen did not return, Gadianton feared he would be destroyed and caused the band to follow him.
The band fled the land by a secret way into the wilderness; Helaman’s searchers could not find them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gadianton and the band may be shown fleeing into the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The route and appearance of the wilderness are unspecified.

narration.text: they took their flight out of the land, by a secret way, into the wilderness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The failed search is reported, not a separate encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict searchers confronting the band.
Do not invent the secret route.

title: The record’s closing note
summary: The forty-second year of the judges ends. An editorial note promises more about Gadianton, describes his role in the near-destruction of the people of Nephi, and clarifies that the referenced ending belongs to the book of Nephi, not Helaman.

explicit_facts.text: More about Gadianton will be spoken hereafter, and the forty-second year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi ended.
The editorial note states that Gadianton proved the overthrow, almost the entire destruction, of the people of Nephi.
The referenced ending is that of the book of Nephi, not the book of Helaman; the narrator took the written account from the book of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A narration-only presentation avoids staging events that these verses merely reference.
unspecified_visual_details: No physical setting, visible narrator, writing activity, or appearance of a record is specified.

narration.text: And more of this Gadianton shall be spoken hereafter.
this Gadianton did prove the overthrow, yea, almost the entire destruction of the people of Nephi.
Behold I do not mean the end of the book of Helaman, but I mean the end of the book of Nephi,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses provide editorial commentary rather than a physically staged encounter.
The reference to destruction must remain narration, not an enacted event.
First-person narration does not establish the narrator’s physical presence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the destruction as occurring in this scene.
Do not add a visible narrator, Gadianton, or record-keeper.
Do not invent a setting, writing action, or dialogue.
Do not combine the year’s ending and the referenced destruction into one simultaneous event.
